title: Does Poincare geometry reduce multi-hop hallucination in biomedical KG retrieval?
motivation: Exploratory observation from the 16-d, curvature-1, 60-epoch run (seeds 7-101): Poincare top-1 answers on 3-hop test queries were path-supported more often than Euclidean answers in 5/5 seeds (mean +0.133, 95% CI [-0.043, 0.309]); on 2-hop they were less often supported (-0.090). This sweep tests whether the 3-hop effect is real and whether it grows in the regime where hyperbolic geometry is expected to help (low dimension, higher curvature, longer training).
definition_hop_hallucination: HHR@1 = fraction of queries whose top-1 compound has no exact typed path from the query in the training graph. Unsupported@10 = mean fraction of the top-10 compounds without such a path.
primary_hypothesis: H1: on 3-hop test queries, Poincare retrieval has a different (expected: lower) HHR@1 than Euclidean retrieval of the same dimension.
primary_test: For each of the 8 Poincare configurations (dims 2,4,8,16 x curvature 1,10) versus the Euclidean model of the same dimension: two-sided paired t-test over the 10 seeds on per-seed 3-hop test HHR@1; Holm-Bonferroni correction across the 8 comparisons at alpha 0.05. Exact two-sided sign test reported alongside.
secondary_outcomes: 3-hop test MRR (accuracy must be reported next to hallucination; a lower HHR with lower MRR is not an improvement)
Effect of typed-path verification reranking on HHR@1 and MRR for both geometries
Sensitivity analysis: primary test restricted to the 5 seeds never inspected before (211, 307, 401, 503, 601)

fixed_settings.lr_selection: per configuration, highest mean of 2-hop and 3-hop validation MRR on the tuning seed

curvature_implementation: Models are trained on the ball of radius 1/sqrt(c). For evaluation, vectors are multiplied by sqrt(c); geodesic distances then scale by 1/sqrt(c) and origin log/exp maps commute with the scaling, so rankings equal those of the curvature-c model.
